**Reporte de situación N.º 22**  
**Terremotos en Venezuela**  
**15 de julio de 2026**  
**Hora: 9:00 pm**

**Destacados**

- Tras los sismos de magnitud 7,2 y 7,5 del 24 de junio (18:00 hora local), l**as autoridades reportan más de 1.200 réplicas.**
- Balance oficial: **4.829 personas fallecidas y 16.740 heridas.**
- **Se lanzó un llamamiento adicional por US$299 millones para ampliar la respuesta a los terremotos y atender las necesidades de**  
    **1,3 millones de personas durante los próximos seis meses.**
- El Sistema de Naciones Unidas y sus organizaciones socias, en coordinación con el gobierno, responden con acciones multisectoriales y continuarán ampliando la asistencia a las personas afectadas.

**Situación general**

Venezuela enfrenta una emergencia nacional tras dos sismos consecutivos de gran magnitud (7,2 y 7,5) ocurridos el 24 de junio (18:00, hora local) en la región centro-norte, con epicentro sobre el eje San Felipe - Yumare - Montalbán (Yaracuy/Carabobo). **Las autoridades reportan 1.284 réplicas.**

A 21 días de los terremotos, las autoridades reportan un balance de **4.829 personas fallecidas y 16.740 personas heridas desde el inicio de la emergencia.** Asimismo, indicaron que **17.907 personas perdieron sus viviendas.**

La respuesta gubernamental mantiene el foco en las labores de búsqueda, la gestión de los campamentos transitorios y la atención de las personas afectadas. Naciones Unidas y sus organizaciones socias, en articulación con las autoridades, realizan acciones multisectoriales para las personas afectadas y continuarán ampliando la respuesta. El Subsecretario General de las Naciones Unidas para Asuntos Humanitarios y Coordinador del Socorro de Emergencia, Tom Fletcher, **anunció una adenda al Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria por 299 millones de dólares, destinada a atender las necesidades multisectoriales de 1,3 millones de personas durante los próximos seis meses.** Este llamado se suma a la meta de 5,5 millones de personas que ya contemplaba atenderse con el Plan este 2026, para lo que se requieren 632 millones de dólares.

La respuesta gubernamental mantiene el foco en las labores de búsqueda, la gestión de los campamentos
transitorios y la atención de las personas afectadas. Naciones Unidas y sus organizaciones socias, en
articulación con las autoridades, realizan acciones multisectoriales para las personas afectadas y
continuarán ampliando la respuesta. El Subsecretario General de las Naciones Unidas para Asuntos
Humanitarios y Coordinador del Socorro de Emergencia, Tom Fletcher, anunció una adenda al Plan de
Respuesta Humanitaria por 299 millones de dólares, destinada a atender las necesidades
multisectoriales de 1,3 millones de personas durante los próximos seis meses. Este llamado se
suma a la meta de 5,5 millones de personas que ya contemplaba atenderse con el Plan este 2026, para
lo que se requieren 632 millones de dólares.
Impacto en infraestructura
 Las autoridades reportan al menos 856 edificios afectados, incluidos 190 edificios colapsados.
 Como parte de la planificación para la recuperación y reconstrucción, las autoridades identificaron
40 terrenos en el estado La Guaira, equivalentes a aproximadamente 584.000 metros cuadrados,
para el desarrollo de proyectos habitacionales destinados a la población afectada.
 Una primera evaluación de la Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Reducción del Riesgo de
Desastres (UNDRR) señala que los daños directos a viviendas e infraestructura suman unos 37 mil
millones de dólares. La mayoría, unos 24 mil millones de dólares, se concentrarían en viviendas,
Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 2
comercios, escuelas, hospitales e instalaciones públicas. Entre tanto, estimaciones preliminares de
PNUD indican daños físicos directos por 6.700 millones de dólares, equivalentes al 6 % del PIB.
Respuesta nacional
 La respuesta gubernamental se mantiene centrada en las labores de búsqueda y rescate, así como
en la atención de las personas afectadas.
 De acuerdo con las autoridades, la respuesta continúa con 106 campamentos transitorios para
la atención de personas afectadas, con capacidad para 25.351 personas y una ocupación de
20.857 personas. Hasta el 15 de julio, 40 campamentos se encuentran instalados en Caracas, 28
en Miranda, 28 en La Guaira, y 10 en Aragua.
 Las autoridades avanzan en un proceso de registro único de las familias afectadas en campamentos
transitorios, mediante la recopilación de datos biométricos y de contacto para apoyar la gestión de
la asistencia, los programas de apoyo social y las soluciones habitacionales.
 El Gobierno venezolano anunció la creación de un fondo inicial de reconstrucción equivalente a 200
millones de dólares.
 Disponible la línea de apoyo psicológico para las personas afectadas: 0800-AYUDA-01.
 Se habilitó un formulario digital del Consejo Nacional para las Personas con Discapacidad
(Conapdis) para coordinar una respuesta oportuna e inclusiva en las zonas afectadas.
 Se habilitaron mecanismos para la localización de personas desaparecidas
(www.localizapacientes.com) y el reporte de personas afectadas (0-800-RESCATE).
 Las actividades escolares permanecen suspendidas en los municipios afectados de los estados
Aragua (Santiago Mariño, Girardot, Ocumare de la Costa de Oro y Tovar); Carabobo (Juan José
Mora, Puerto Cabello, Naguanagua y Valencia); Falcón (José Laurencio Silva); La Guaira (Vargas);
Distrito Capital (Libertador); y Miranda (Chacao, Baruta, El Hatillo, Sucre, Plaza, Zamora, Acevedo,
Brión, Buroz, Páez, Andrés Bello y Pedro Gual).
Situación por estado
Distrito Capital (Caracas) y Miranda
 Se realizó una reunión con autoridades de la Gobernación de Miranda y miembros de Interclúster
para compartir los resultados del levantamiento de necesidades multisectoriales en siete
campamentos visitados. Se presentaron las líneas de respuesta y se acordó llevar a cabo el
fortalecimiento de capacidades para los coordinadores/as y personal de primera línea de los
campamentos transitorios desde los distintos clústeres.
Acciones de respuesta: Organizaciones como Tinta Violeta, FUNDANA y World Vision se encuentran
brindando apoyo en el área de protección a familias afectadas, especialmente a nivel psicosocial.
La Guaira
 Las autoridades y organizaciones humanitarias continúan fortaleciendo la respuesta en los
campamentos transitorios de La Guaira mediante la ampliación de servicios multisectoriales, la
mejora de las condiciones de alojamiento y la gestión coordinada de la asistencia. Continúan las
distribuciones de artículos esenciales, asistencia alimentaria, actividades de protección,
intervenciones de salud y apoyo psicosocial, así como las acciones para mejorar el acceso a agua
segura, saneamiento, conectividad e infraestructura comunitaria.
Carabobo y Yaracuy (zona del epicentro)
 En Yaracuy, particularmente en el municipio Veroes y otras localidades cercanas a la zona
epicentral, se reportan viviendas destruidas o en condición de alto riesgo. Se identifican
necesidades prioritarias en protección, salud mental y apoyo psicosocial, salud, alojamiento, agua,
saneamiento e higiene (ASH) y seguridad alimentaria.
Acciones de respuesta: Cinco (5) organizaciones (Cruz Roja Venezolana, CESAP, Tierra Viva, Cáritas
Morón y Empodérame) brindan respuesta en salud, alimentación, agua y distribución de ayuda
humanitaria.
Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 3
Falcón (Tucacas – Municipio Silva)
 El Foro Local de Coordinación (FLC) mantiene el seguimiento de posibles necesidades de apoyo
complementario para los grupos familiares desplazados desde La Guaira y Caracas. En
coordinación con UNICEF, se analizó la situación en el municipio Silva, destacándose la necesidad
de intervenciones sostenibles y complementarias.
 OCHA y la Secretaría General de Gobierno facilitaron una reunión interinstitucional para identificar
prioridades de acción complementaria en agua, saneamiento e higiene (ASH), salud, nutrición,
planificación familiar, saneamiento ambiental y medios de vida. Como resultado, UNICEF evaluará
posibles áreas de intervención.
Acciones de respuesta: Se da continuidad al ciclo de capacitaciones del Clúster de Protección y a las
jornadas de ASH y apoyo psicosocial en Boca de Aroa y Palmasola, implementadas por ACH, Azul
Positivo, la OIM, Centroccidente, ODISEF y AVSI en coordinación con las autoridades regionales.
Otros estados
 Apure: Se mantiene el acumulado de unas 250 personas desplazadas procedentes del litoral
central. El Foro Local de Coordinación (FLC) continúa realizando monitoreo y provee atenciones
multisectoriales, incluidos primeros auxilios psicológicos.
 Bolívar: Representantes de la comunidad humanitaria y de la Gobernación coordinaron acciones
para fortalecer la respuesta a las personas desplazadas desde las zonas afectadas por los
terremotos. Entre las principales prioridades identificadas destacan el fortalecimiento de
capacidades técnicas del personal de atención y el apoyo especializado en atención psicosocial.
Según cifras oficiales, se han registrado y caracterizado 63 familias (198 personas): 42 en Caroní,
15 en Angostura del Orinoco, tres en Padre Pedro Chien, dos en Cedeño y una en Piar. Las familias
identificadas han recibido atención inicial, incluida la caracterización de necesidades, primeros
auxilios psicológicos, servicios de salud y apoyo para la regularización de documentos de identidad.
 Delta Amacuro: Autoridades y socios humanitarios revisaron las acciones de preparación y
respuesta para las familias movilizadas desde las zonas afectadas por los terremotos. El PMA prevé
suministrar asistencia alimentaria inmediata para las primeras 72 horas, Cáritas Delta Amacuro
podría apoyar con kits de higiene y World Vision con canastas alimentarias para hogares con niñas
y niños. Asimismo, los actores humanitarios coordinarán actividades de fortalecimiento de
capacidades y gestión de información para apoyar el registro, seguimiento y atención de la
población movilizada hacia el estado.
 Zulia: Se mantiene activo el punto de triaje médico y orientación para las familias en movilidad en
el terminal de pasajeros de Maracaibo, en articulación con la Cruz Roja Venezolana y ASONACOP.
Los reportes del 14 de julio dan cuenta de una tendencia a la disminución de la movilidad, con la
atención de grupos familiares procedentes de Catia La Mar y La Guaira, con destino a Maracaibo o
en tránsito hacia Colombia (Cartagena).
 En los estados Monagas, Anzoátegui, Nueva Esparta, Trujillo y Lara se mantienen las acciones de
coordinación, acopio y monitoreo previamente informadas. Los Foros Local de Coordinación
mantienen el seguimiento a la atención y los riesgos de protección de la población en movilidad.
Coordinación humanitaria
 OCHA, junto con el Coordinador Humanitario y en articulación con las autoridades nacionales,
continúa coordinando la respuesta humanitaria con las Naciones Unidas y organizaciones socias,
priorizando acciones en salud, alojamiento, alimentación, ASH, logística y protección.
 UNDAC y OCHA continuaron apoyando a Protección Civil en el fortalecimiento de capacidades de
coordinación y gestión de información para emergencias, incluyendo intercambio técnico sobre
mecanismos de coordinación USAR y herramientas de seguimiento operativo.
 En total, 71 equipos de búsqueda y rescate de 31 países, con 2.786 efectivos y 216 perros, se
desplegaron en las zonas más afectadas para apoyar labores de rescate. Esto incluye equipos en
proceso de desmovilización.
Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 4
 OCHA continuó fortaleciendo la coordinación con el sector privado para apoyar las acciones de
respuesta y recuperación temprana, promoviendo la articulación con actores especializados en
áreas como logística, gestión de escombros, rehabilitación de infraestructura y planificación de la
reconstrucción, a través de los mecanismos de coordinación existentes entre las Naciones Unidas
y el sector privado.
 Autoridades venezolanas solicitaron la activación de la Evaluación de las Necesidades Posteriores
al Desastre (PDNA), en el marco del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas y con el acompañamiento del
PNUD. Conforme a la metodología internacional de la PDNA, se avanzará en las coordinaciones
correspondientes con las contrapartes relevantes.
 Se informó la activación de un mecanismo especial para la tramitación expedita de una “Visa de
Trabajo para Situaciones Especiales”, gestionada a través del Ministerio del Poder Popular para
Relaciones Exteriores. El procedimiento podrá realizarse en línea, bajo la coordinación del
Despacho del Viceministro para Temas Multilaterales y la Oficina de Relaciones Consulares, y
estará dirigido a trabajadores extranjeros de organizaciones internacionales, así como a
funcionarios de las Naciones Unidas, que se desplieguen en Venezuela en el marco de la respuesta
a la emergencia ocasionada por los terremotos.
Acciones iniciales de Respuesta Humanitaria
Seguridad Alimentaria
 El PMA continúa ampliando progresivamente su respuesta, proporcionando asistencia alimentaria
esencial más allá del estado La Guaira. Si bien La Guaira ha sido el estado más afectado, otros
estados, incluidos Miranda, Yaracuy, Falcón, Carabobo y Aragua, también enfrentan las
consecuencias de los terremotos. En este contexto, el 15 de julio el PMA realizó su primera
distribución en el estado Miranda, alcanzando a 1.160 personas afectadas en las parroquias
Higuerote, Curiepe y Tacarigua.
 Además, el PMA mantiene la asistencia en La Guaira mediante distribución de alimentos,
proporcionando canastas alimentarias a 4.348 personas en comunidades afectadas y sirviendo
7.358 comidas calientes a personas alojadas en los campamentos transitorios coordinados por
Naciones Unidas. El PMA continuará ampliando el alcance de la respuesta mientras mantiene la
asistencia a las personas más afectadas por los terremotos. Desde el inicio de la respuesta a la
emergencia, el PMA ha brindado asistencia alimentaria a 73.228 personas.
Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene
 UNICEF y sus socios suministran diariamente unos 80.000 litros de agua segura en los tres
campamentos transitorios identificados en La Guaira, beneficiando a aproximadamente 3.500
personas.
 Además, en los campamentos transitorios identificados en La Guaira, UNICEF mantuvo y adecuó
lavaderos y puntos de lavado de manos, garantizó la limpieza de baños portátiles y reforzó las
condiciones de saneamiento mediante puntos de lavado de ropa, puntos de lavado de manos,
servicios sanitarios y almacenamiento de agua. Además, realizó actividades de promoción de
higiene que alcanzaron a 772 personas.
Alojamiento, Energía y Enseres
 ACNUR fortaleció las condiciones de alojamiento y protección en los campamentos transitorios
Polideportivo José María Vargas, Estadio César Nieves, Playa Grande y Mare Abajo mediante la
distribución de 539 kits de lámparas solares y mosquiteros, 200 linternas solares y la instalación
de 132 reflectores solares y otras estructuras temporales para mejorar la iluminación y la seguridad
en áreas comunitarias, zonas de baños y espacios de alojamiento.
 En los campamentos transitorios de La Guaira continuaron las acciones de coordinación,
alojamiento y provisión de servicios multisectoriales. En el campamento Polideportivo José María
Vargas, la OIM mantuvo la asistencia a 347 familias, actualizó los registros de población y coordinó
procesos de reubicación hacia refugios en Caracas. Asimismo, funcionarios gubernamentales,
representantes diplomáticos y del Sistema de Naciones Unidas realizaron visitas de seguimiento a
Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 5
los campamentos Polideportivo José María Vargas y Playa Grande para revisar las condiciones de
atención y las necesidades de la población afectada.
 En el campamento transitorio Playa Grande se avanzó en la planificación para la reubicación del
campamento hacia la Unidad Educativa República del Salvador y se mantuvieron servicios de
salud, protección, alimentación y agua, saneamiento e higiene (ASH).
 En el campamento transitorio Campo de Golf (Tanaguarena), la OIM distribuyó 50 kits de artículos
no alimentarios, avanzó en la coordinación para la instalación de espacios destinados a la provisión
de servicios humanitarios y desarrolló actividades de sensibilización sobre convivencia segura y
prevención de la trata de personas.
 En el campamento transitorio Mare Abajo II, las organizaciones humanitarias fortalecieron la
coordinación interagencial para mejorar la complementariedad de servicios. Continuaron las
mejoras de infraestructura para alojamiento y saneamiento, incluyendo la instalación de literas,
adecuaciones en las carpas, construcción de duchas y drenajes, así como la prestación de
servicios de salud, alimentación y ASH para la población afectada.
Logística y Telecomunicaciones
 El PMA, a través del Grupo de Trabajo de Logística (GTL), apoyó el transporte desde el Aeropuerto
Internacional de Maiquetía hasta los almacenes del GTL en La Guaira de 37.93 TM de insumos de
agua, saneamiento e higiene y refugio de la Federación Internacional de Sociedades de la Cruz
Roja y de la Media Luna Roja.
Nutrición
 UNICEF instaló tres espacios de apoyo a la lactancia materna en tres campamentos transitorios,
donde se brinda orientación y asistencia a madres lactantes.
 En el campamento transitorio César Nieves, UNICEF realizó tamizaje nutricional a niños, niñas y
adolescentes y brindó apoyo a mujeres embarazadas.
Protección (incluidos Áreas de Responsabilidad de Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes y Violencia
Basada en Género)
 Hasta el 15 de julio, ACNUR ha alcanzado a 875 personas en los campamentos transitorios
Polideportivo José María Vargas, Estadio César Nieves y Playa Grande mediante asistencia legal,
gestión de casos, apoyo psicosocial, orientación y derivaciones a servicios especializados.
Asimismo, 136 niñas, niños y adolescentes y sus familias recibieron orientación sobre registro de
nacimiento, documentación de identidad y representación legal, complementada con
acompañamiento psicosocial y socioemocional para fortalecer estrategias de afrontamiento frente
a los efectos de los terremotos.
 UNFPA mantuvo actividades de sensibilización sobre violencia basada en género (VBG) e higiene
menstrual en el campamento transitorio César Nieves, complementadas con la distribución de 16
kits de dignidad para adolescentes.
 UNICEF y sus socios brindaron apoyo psicosocial a 132 niños, niñas y adolescentes y a 55 madres,
padres y cuidadores a través de Espacios Amigables y sesiones grupales en los campamentos
transitorios de Polideportivo J.M. Vargas, César Nieves y Playa Grande.
Salud
 UNICEF apoyó la aplicación de 76 dosis de vacunas en los campamentos transitorios Polideportivo
Vargas (44) y César Nieves (32). En el campamento transitorio Playa Grande, a través del
Ministerio del Poder Popular para la Salud, brindó atención básica de salud a 32 personas.
 UNFPA reportó actividades en los campamentos transitorios César Nieves, Playa Grande y
Polideportivo el 15 de julio, incluyendo 143 sesiones de sensibilización y 32 consultas prenatales,
de las cuales 31 se realizaron en Polideportivo y una en Cesar Nieves. Asimismo, se distribuyeron
100 métodos anticonceptivos modernos (MAC), incluidos 91 implantes subdérmicos, siete
inyectables y dos anticonceptivos orales.
Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para la Coordinación de Asuntos Humanitarios (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 6
 En el campamento transitorio Playa Grande, se brindaron 147 atenciones médicas por parte de
Project HOPE y Ven Da Tu Mano.
 International Medical Corps (IMC) mantiene desplegadas Unidades Médicas Móviles y un Equipo
Médico de Emergencia (EMT Tipo 1) en el estado La Guaira, brindando atención primaria de salud,
salud sexual y reproductiva y salud mental y apoyo psicosocial (SMAPS), además de apoyar el
acceso a agua segura mediante el suministro de agua potable. Entre el 1 y el 14 de julio, IMC
realizó 1.586 consultas en comunidades afectadas. Las principales causas de atención fueron
enfermedades no transmisibles (47%) y enfermedades transmisibles (38%), seguidas por servicios
de salud mental y apoyo psicosocial (6%), salud sexual y reproductiva (6%) y atención de
traumatismos y lesiones (3%), evidenciando una demanda sostenida de servicios esenciales de
salud en las zonas afectadas.
Financiamiento humanitario y contribuciones
 El jefe humanitario de Naciones Unidas, Tom Fletcher, anunció una adenda al Plan de Respuesta
Humanitaria para Venezuela. Este llamado contempla las necesidades multisectoriales de 1,3
millones de personas por los próximos seis meses. Para alcanzar a estas personas, se necesitan
299 millones de dólares, que se suman a los 632 millones de dólares solicitados al inicio del año.
 OIM lanzó un llamamiento por 98 millones de dólares para asistir a 850.000 personas y 140
entidades los próximos seis meses. La OPS/OMS lanzó un llamamiento de emergencia por casi 24

dólares para apoyar a hasta 30.000 personas afectadas durante los próximos seis meses.
 La Unión Europea anunció este 15 de julio una contribución adicional de 20 millones de euros
para apoyar la acción humanitaria en el país. De este total, 10 millones de euros estarán
destinados a apoyar operaciones de búsqueda y rescate, asistencia médica y el despliegue
de otros expertos, así como asistencia material, en el país. Esta contribución se suma a los 5

 Además, como parte del puente aéreo humanitario de la Unión Europea, puesto en marcha en junio,

documents.title: Venezuela: UNOPS apoyará a las comunidades afectadas por los recientes terremotos
documents.body_text:
***CARACAS, 15 de julio de 2026.—*** UNOPS acaba de concluir una misión en Venezuela para apoyar los esfuerzos de respuesta y recuperación tras el devastador terremoto.

**Dalila Gonçalves, Directora Regional de UNOPS para América Latina y el Caribe**, encabezó la misión. Mantuvo conversaciones con el gobierno, representantes del sector privado y socios internacionales para identificar posibles áreas de cooperación en la recuperación temprana y la respuesta humanitaria.

"Nuestra solidaridad está con el pueblo de Venezuela. Las necesidades de las comunidades son inmensas y los daños son colosales. Fuimos testigos de primera mano de edificios enteros destruidos, incluyendo hogares, escuelas y centros de salud. Continuaremos trabajando con nuestros socios para identificar áreas de cooperación y apoyar la recuperación de las comunidades, la entrega de asistencia tan necesaria y la reconstrucción de los servicios de infraestructura dañados", señaló **Gonçalves**.

**FIN**

documents.title: Venezuela: UNOPS to support communities impacted by the recent earthquakes
documents.body_text:
**CARACAS, 15 July 2026.—** UNOPS has just concluded a mission to Venezuela to support response recovery efforts following the devastating earthquake.

**Dalila Gonçalves**, **UNOPS Regional Director for Latin America and the Caribbean**, led the mission. She engagedin discussions with the government, private-sector representatives, and international partners to identify potential areas of cooperation in early recovery and humanitarian response.

"Our solidarity is with the people of Venezuela. The communities’ needs are immense and the damage is colossal. We witnessed first hand whole buildings smashed including people’s homes, schools and healthcare facilities. We will continue to work with partners to identify areas of cooperation and support the communities’ recovery, the delivery of much needed assistance and the reconstruction of damaged infrastructure services”, said  **Gonçalves**.

**ENDs**

documents.title: Venezuela: Earthquakes - LTC Situation Report (Telecoms) #03 (Reporting period: 08 - 14 July 2026)
documents.body_text:
*This Situation Report provides an overview of the twin earthquakes that struck Venezuela on 24 June 2026 (magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5), and their impact on telecommunications. It outlines the activities of the WFP-led Logistics and Telecommunications Cluster (LTC)1 Telecoms Area in supporting emergency communications for the humanitarian response. The Cluster is currently not formally activated for this emergency.*

**Summary Points**

• LTC Telecoms is coordinating telecommunications response efforts in Venezuela, working with government authorities, mobile network operators, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), and other partners to identify connectivity gaps, restore critical communications, and prioritize support in the most affected areas.

• LTC Telecoms and partners expanded emergency connectivity services at priority displacement sites, including Playa Grande, César Nieves Stadium Transitional Camp, and Caraballeda, providing shared internet access and strengthening communications for affected communities and humanitarian responders.

• Despite ongoing restoration efforts, power disruptions, damaged telecommunications infrastructure, and connectivity challenges continue to affect communities in La Guaira, Petare, Catia, and other earthquake-affected areas, underscoring the need for continued telecommunications support.

LTC Situation Report (Telecoms) #03
Reporting period: 08 – 14 July 2026
This Situation Report provides an overview of the twin earthquakes that struck Venezuela on 24 June 2026
(magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5), and their impact on telecommunications. It outlines the activities of the WFP-led
Logistics and Telecommunications Cluster (LTC)1 Telecoms Area in supporting emergency communications for
the humanitarian response. The Cluster is currently not formally activated for this emergency.

• LTC Telecoms is coordinating telecommunications
response efforts in Venezuela, working with

the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian

and prioritize support in the most affected areas.

and other earthquake-affected areas, underscoring
the need for continued telecommunications support.
Situation Overview
Between 08 and 13 July, Venezuela remained in a severe humanitarian emergency following the twin
magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 earthquakes that struck the north-central region on 24 June, just 40 seconds
apart. The earthquakes affected at least seven states, including La Guaira, Capital District, Miranda,
Aragua, Carabobo, Falcón, and Yaracuy, causing widespread damage to homes, public infrastructure,
schools, hospitals, electricity and telecommunications networks, and other essential services.
The response continues to transition from large-scale search and rescue operations to humanitarian
relief, emergency shelter, protection services, health support, and early recovery planning. Recurrent
aftershocks continued to generate fear among affected communities and disrupt response efforts. By
1 The ETC and Logistics Cluster have been merged into the Logistics and Telecommunications Cluster (LTC), following the humanitarian reset in 2025.
Bringing logistics and emergency telecommunications under one coordination structure, the WFP-led LTC is the backbone of the entire humanitarian
response, enabling humanitarian action to move, communicate, coordinate, and deliver lifesaving assistance.
Page 1 of 5
Logistics and Telecommunications Cluster (LTC) – Telecoms Area www.ETCluster.org | www.LOGcluster.org

10 July, authorities had recorded more than 1,100 aftershocks, highlighting the ongoing seismic risk.
The humanitarian situation remained severe, with casualty figures continuing to rise and assessments
identifying significant multisectoral needs affecting an estimated 1.3 million people.
OCHA continued coordinating international assistance and supporting response efforts. Priority needs
include emergency shelter, medical care, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services, food
assistance, child protection, and the restoration of telecommunications and other critical infrastructure.
During the reporting period, UN Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher concluded a four-day visit
to Venezuela, calling for sustained international support to meet urgent humanitarian needs and
support recovery efforts.
Authorities maintained emergency coordination mechanisms and continued managing transitional
camps across affected areas. While responsibility for urban search and rescue activities was
increasingly transferred to Venezuelan Civil Protection authorities, international response teams
remained deployed to support recovery efforts, assessments, and humanitarian operations.
Telecommunications Overview
The 24 June earthquakes caused significant damage to telecommunications infrastructure across La
Guaira, Greater Caracas, and parts of Miranda, Carabobo, Yaracuy, Aragua, and Falcón States. While
Venezuela's core telecommunications networks remain operational, damage to power systems, fibre-
optic infrastructure, mobile network facilities, and transmission equipment disrupted connectivity in
several affected areas. Ongoing aftershocks, infrastructure damage, and access constraints continued
to affect service reliability and restoration efforts.
Although emergency repairs restored partial services in major population centres, intermittent outages
and reduced service quality persisted in some earthquake-affected areas. Reliable telecommunications
services remained critical to humanitarian operations, enabling coordination among responders,
information sharing, and access to assistance for affected communities.
Mobile network operators Compañía Anónima Nacional Teléfonos de Venezuela (CANTV), Movistar,
and Digitel remained operational across most of the country; however, localized service disruptions
and reduced network performance continued to be reported in affected areas. Restoration efforts
remained ongoing as authorities and service providers worked to repair damaged infrastructure and
stabilize connectivity.
The electricity sector continued to face operational challenges due to damage to transmission and
distribution infrastructure. Power disruptions affected households, health facilities, water systems,
telecommunications equipment, and temporary displacement sites, slowing recovery efforts and
complicating the restoration of essential services.
Continued investment in telecommunications and power infrastructure repairs, alongside emergency
connectivity solutions, will be critical to restoring reliable communications, supporting humanitarian
operations, and enabling longer-term recovery in earthquake-affected communities.
LTC Telecoms Activities
Coordination
Page 2 of 5
Logistics and Telecommunications Cluster (LTC) – Telecoms Area www.ETCluster.org | www.LOGcluster.org

Since 05 July, an LTC Telecoms Coordinator has been deployed to Caracas to support inter-agency
coordination, telecommunications assessments, and the restoration of critical communications
services. Working with OCHA, Comisión Nacional de Telecomunicaciones (CONATEL), CANTV,
Movistar, Digitel, and other partners, LTC Telecoms is supporting the establishment of a
telecommunications coordination mechanism to map incoming assets, identify connectivity gaps, avoid
duplication, and prioritize support in the most affected areas.
As of 13 July, efforts remain focused on high-impact locations including Petare, Catia, and La Guaira,
where power outages, network disruptions, and infrastructure damage continue to affect connectivity.
Planned and ongoing interventions include shared internet services, public Wi-Fi, satellite
communications, and solar-powered charging facilities to support humanitarian coordination,
information-sharing, and access to services.
Since 03 July, LTC Telecoms has been conducting a rapid telecommunications and connectivity
survey across affected areas. The assessment is mapping available connectivity services, including
mobile, fibre, VSAT, BGAN, and Starlink connectivity, to identify service gaps and prioritize locations
for shared connectivity solutions.
ICT assessments
On 09 July, LTC Telecoms conducted an ICT assessment at Playa Verde, a displacement site in La
Guaira, to identify connectivity and power requirements. The assessment found limited access to
reliable electricity and internet connectivity, and LTC Telecoms plans to install shared internet and
power solutions to support site operations and affected communities.
Playa Verde is the fourth priority site assessed following Playa Grande, César Nieves Stadium
Transitional Camp, and Polideportivo José María Vargas Stadium.
Internet connectivity
On 07 and 08 July, LTC Telecoms installed Starlink connectivity systems with solar panels, battery
backup, and Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) systems at Playa Grande and César Nieves Stadium
Transitional Camp. These deployments strengthened communications and connectivity services for
approximately 1,850 people across both sites.
To support the emergency response, SpaceX activated its disaster response programme, making
Starlink connectivity kits available for deployment in affected areas under temporary emergency
arrangements approved by national authorities.
Services for communities
Community connectivity services are being established in priority displacement sites through
collaboration between emergency.lu, CONATEL, G-Networks, WFP, and other response partners. Using
fibre connectivity and wireless distribution networks, the solution enables affected communities to
communicate with family members, access information, and maintain essential digital services during
the emergency.
As of 13 July, community connectivity networks had been installed at Caraballeda and César Nieves
Stadium Transitional Camp, providing internet access for affected populations and humanitarian
responders. Installation at Playa Grande is scheduled for 15 July.
On 13 July, emergency.lu transferred the community connectivity solution to WFP. Discussions are
ongoing with service providers to maintain services throughout the response and recovery period.
Following the completion of its mission, emergency.lu departed Venezuela on 14 July. The deployment
Page 3 of 5
Logistics and Telecommunications Cluster (LTC) – Telecoms Area www.ETCluster.org | www.LOGcluster.org

was carried out through the United Nations Disaster Assessment and Coordination (UNDAC) system as
part of the European Civil Protection Mechanism and is co-funded by the European Union (EU).
Secure communications
On 28 June, {TESS+} contacted UNDSS Venezuela to verify the operational status of the Security
Communications Systems (SCS), including radio networks. As of 13 July, the SCS remains operational;
however, intermittent internet connectivity persists in some heavily affected locations. UNDSS is
working with WFP to restore stable connectivity in the affected locations.
Information Management
A dedicated LTC Telecoms emergency operations page was established to provide operational
updates and response information.
Visit the LTC Telecoms Dashboard for an overview of planned and active services.
LTC Telecoms and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) activated the Disaster
Connectivity Map (DCM) on 25 June to monitor connectivity impacts across affected areas. The DCM
is integrated into LogIE for Venezuela to support operational planning.
The DCM showed national connectivity dropping from more than 90 percent to approximately 59–65
percent immediately following the earthquakes before partially recovering to around 77 percent within
24–48 hours. As of 13 July, La Guaira remained the most affected area, while connectivity in Caracas
had largely recovered. Service disruptions continued to affect parts of Yaracuy and Carabobo States.
Additional IM support is being provided by MapAction and Kobo Toolbox for mapping, data collection,
analysis, and information-sharing activities.
Funding
Donor engagement remains ongoing as humanitarian funding requirements are consolidated under the
forthcoming Flash Appeal.
The US Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance (BHA) has committed USD 9 million, with a further USD 6
million under processing, bringing the expected total contribution to USD 15 million. Funding is
primarily focused on humanitarian supply chain operations and the delivery of emergency assistance.
The Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) has allocated USD 15 million for the earthquake
response, of which approximately USD 2 million is expected to be allocated to WFP.
Meetings
A Global LTC Telecoms Partner Teleconference was held on 13 July at 14:00 UTC to support
information exchange and coordination. Minutes of the meeting are available here.
Page 4 of 5
Logistics and Telecommunications Cluster (LTC) – Telecoms Area www.ETCluster.org | www.LOGcluster.org

LTC Logistics Area
For more information on the logistics component of the LTC response, a dedicated Venezuela logistics
webpage is available here with the latest updates on working group meetings, key documents, maps,
and available support.
The latest LTC Logistics Situation Report is available here.
Challenges
Equipment security: Connectivity equipment remains exposed in several locations. In the absence of
secure storage, equipment must be dismantled each evening and reinstalled each morning, increasing
the risk of damage, loss, delayed start-up, and service interruptions.
Power reliability: Power supply remains fragile across operational sites. Backup solutions, including
UPS units, generators, EcoFlow batteries, and solar panels, remain essential to maintain service
continuity during outages.
Connectivity congestion: High numbers of Starlink units and unmanaged routers may reduce service
quality and affect community access.
Fuel movement restrictions: Generator operations are constrained by challenges associated with
transporting fuel between sites.
Evolving site requirements: Population growth at existing sites and the emergence of new locations,
such as Playa Verde, require continuous reassessment of connectivity and power needs.

documents.title: Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of): Earthquake Response Situation Report #12 (13 to 14 July 2026)
documents.body_text:
The twelfth Situation Report provides an update on IOM’s response to the 24 June earthquakes in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, covering the period from 13 to 14 July.

**Highlights**

Between 13 and 14 July, IOM continued scaling up its multisectoral response in transitory camps and affected communities in La Guaira, with interventions in shelter and site coordination, health, protection, water, sanitation and hygiene, and information management.

To date, IOM has reached 5,774 unique individuals through 8,844 instances of assistance and services, mainly in health and MHPSS, shelter and site coordination, WASH, and protection.

IOM distributed essential items, advanced the installation and organization of transitory camps, and supported the relocation of 31 households from the José María Vargas Sports Centre to other accommodation sites in Caracas.

**IOM Activities**

IOM continues supporting transitory camps and affected communities in La Guaira through shelter, site coordination, WASH, health and MHPSS, protection, registration, mobility monitoring and inter-agency coordination.

IOM and its partners distributed 517 tarpaulins, 515 kitchen sets and 476 buckets. At the Tanaguarena Golf Course, 120 essential item kits were distributed and the arrival of large-capacity tents was coordinated. The organization of spaces and services also continued at Mare Abajo II and Playa Grande.

At César Nieves Stadium and Playa Grande, water supply, toilet cleaning, shower installation, waste management and hygiene promotion activities continued.

At the José María Vargas Sports Centre, 14 mobile health sessions have been conducted, reaching a cumulative total of 1,120 consultations. To date, IOM has delivered 4,644 health and MHPSS services as part of the response.

Registration reached 533 families and 1,598 individuals at César Nieves Stadium, and 149 families and 445 individuals at Playa Grande. Monitoring also identified the movement of affected families from La Guaira to Amazonas and Santa Elena de Uairén.

**IOM Planned Response**

IOM will continue strengthening the management and improvement of transitory camps, the installation of tents and basic services, health and mental health care, protection screening and referrals, and measures to prevent sexual exploitation and abuse.

IOM will also continue registration and the monitoring of needs and mobility, as well as support to the Infrastructure and Temporary Accommodation Working Group to consolidate information and coordinate interventions.

documents.title: Venezuela (República Bolivariana de): Respuesta a Terremotos - Reporte de Situación #12 (13 y 14 de julio 2026)
documents.body_text:
El duodécimo Reporte de Situación presenta una actualización sobre la respuesta de la OIM a los terremotos del 24 de junio en la República Bolivariana de Venezuela, con información correspondiente al período del 13 al 14 de julio.

**Aspectos destacados**

Entre el 13 y el 14 de julio, la OIM continuó ampliando su respuesta multisectorial en campamentos transitorios y comunidades afectadas de La Guaira, con intervenciones en alojamiento y coordinación de sitios, salud, protección, agua, saneamiento e higiene, y gestión de información.

A la fecha, la OIM ha alcanzado a 5.774 personas únicas mediante 8.844 asistencias y servicios, principalmente en salud y SMAPS, alojamiento y coordinación de sitios, WASH y protección.

La OIM distribuyó artículos esenciales, avanzó en la instalación y organización de campamentos transitorios y apoyó la reubicación de 31 núcleos familiares desde el Polideportivo José María Vargas hacia otros espacios en Caracas.

**Actividades de la OIM**

La OIM continúa apoyando campamentos transitorios y comunidades afectadas en La Guaira mediante alojamiento, coordinación de sitios, WASH, salud y SMAPS, protección, registro, monitoreo de la movilidad y coordinación interagencial.

La OIM y sus socios distribuyeron 517 lonas, 515 sets de cocina y 476 baldes. En el Campo de Golf de Tanaguarena se entregaron 120 kits de artículos esenciales y se coordinó el ingreso de carpas de gran capacidad. También continuó la organización de espacios y servicios en Mare Abajo II y Playa Grande.

En el Estadio César Nieves y Playa Grande continuaron las actividades de abastecimiento de agua, limpieza de baños, instalación de duchas, gestión de residuos y promoción de la higiene.

En el Polideportivo José María Vargas se han realizado 14 jornadas móviles de salud, con 1.120 consultas acumuladas. A la fecha, la OIM ha prestado 4.644 asistencias y servicios de salud y SMAPS.

El registro alcanzó 533 familias y 1.598 personas en el Estadio César Nieves, y 149 familias y 445 personas en Playa Grande. El monitoreo también identificó la movilidad de familias afectadas desde La Guaira hacia Amazonas y Santa Elena de Uairén.

**Respuesta planificada de la OIM**

La OIM continuará fortaleciendo la gestión y adecuación de campamentos transitorios, la instalación de carpas y servicios básicos, la atención en salud y salud mental, el triaje y las derivaciones de protección, y las medidas de prevención de la explotación y el abuso sexual.

También continuará el registro y monitoreo de necesidades y movilidad, así como el apoyo al Grupo de Trabajo de Infraestructura y Alojamientos Temporales para consolidar información y coordinar las intervenciones.

documents.title: EU provides €20 million in humanitarian funding following earthquakes in Venezuela
sources: European Commission's Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations
documents.body_text:
The European Union is releasing an additional €10 million in humanitarian funding to help the most affected communities in Venezuela, following the recent earthquakes.

The other €10 million, subject to the approval of the Budgetary Authority, support the search and rescue, medical and other expert teams' operations, along with in-kind assistance deployed in the country.

The announcement comes as Commissioner for Preparedness and Crisis Management Hadja **Lahbib** visits Venezuela as a sign of the EU's unwavering support for the country in facing this crisis. The Commissioner will be in Caracas tomorrow, where she will meet with EU-funded aid partners and local authorities that are coordinating the emergency response, as well as with one of the European medical teams deployed through the EU Civil Protection Mechanism.

Today's announcement add to the [€5 million](https://reliefweb.int/news-stories/news/eu-delivers-emergency-aid-and-organises-humanitarian-flight-response-earthquakes-venezuela-2026-06-29_en) life-saving assistance already approved at the end of June, and to the €52 million allocated at the beginning of the year to respond to the humanitarian consequences of the socio-economic crisis in [Venezuela](https://civil-protection-humanitarian-aid.ec.europa.eu/where/latin-america-and-caribbean/venezuela_en). EU humanitarian aid is solely channelled through partners such as UN agencies and international NGOs, which work with local partners.

Additionally, as part of the EU Humanitarian Air Bridge launched in June, 2 EU-funded flights have already landed in Venezuela, bringing nearly 80 tonnes of essential supplies.

Through the EU [Civil Protection Mechanism](https://civil-protection-humanitarian-aid.ec.europa.eu/what/civil-protection/eu-civil-protection-mechanism_en), around 750 responders and experts, as well as relief items, have been mobilised from 18 countries. This includes rescue teams, medicines, shelter and a satellite telecommunication platform. The EU's [Copernicus](https://mapping.emergency.copernicus.eu/activations/EMSR884/) satellite service also provided emergency mapping.

> *'Venezuela may be an ocean away, but the Venezuelan people are close to our hearts. From the very first hours after the earthquakes, the European Union has stood with them'*, Commissioner for Preparedness and Crisis Management, Hadja **Lahbib**, said ahead of her visit. *'And we are stepping up our support. This new funding will help deliver food, clean water, medicines, shelter and other lifesaving assistance to families who have lost everything. I want to thank the emergency responders who have worked day and night, pulling survivors from the rubble and bringing hope when it was needed most.'*

Publication date15 July 2026

documents.title: Earthquakes in Venezuela: Situation Report #21 (14 July 2026, Time: 09:00 pm)
sources: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
documents.body_text:
**Situation Report No. 21**  
**Earthquakes in Venezuela**  
**14 July 2026**  
**Time: 9:00 pm**

**Highlights**

- Following the 24 June earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 (18:00 local time), **authorities report more than 1,200 aftershocks.**
- Official toll: **4,734 people dead and 16,740 injured.**
- A total of **6,462 people have been rescued.**
- **An additional appeal for US$298 million was launched to scale up the earthquake response and address the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.**
- The United Nations system and its partner organizations, in coordination with the Government, are responding with multisectoral actions and will continue to scale up assistance to affected people.

**Situation overview**

Venezuela is facing a national emergency following two consecutive high-magnitude earthquakes (7.2 and 7.5) that struck on 24 June (18:00 local time) in the north-central region, with the epicentre located along the San Felipe–Yumare–Montalbán axis (Yaracuy/Carabobo). **Authorities report 1,275 aftershocks.**

Twenty days since the earthquakes, authorities report a toll of **4,734 people dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462 rescued** since the onset of the emergency. Authorities also indicated that **17,907 people lost their home**.

The Government response remains focused on search operations, the management of transitional camps and assistance to affected populations. The United Nations and its partner organizations, in coordination with the authorities, continue implementing multisectoral response activities and scaling up assistance. United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom Fletcher **announced a US$298 million addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan aimed at addressing the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months.** This is in addition to the 5.5 million people already targeted under the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan, which requires US$632 million in funding.

authorities report a toll of 4,734 people
dead, 16,740 injured and 6,462
rescued since the onset of the
emergency. Authorities also indicated
that 17,907 people lost their home.
The Government response remains focused on search operations, the management of transitional camps
and assistance to affected populations. The United Nations and its partner organizations, in coordination
with the authorities, continue implementing multisectoral response activities and scaling up assistance.
United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator Tom
Fletcher announced a US$298 million addendum to the Humanitarian Response Plan aimed at
addressing the multisectoral needs of 1.3 million people over the next six months. This is in addition
to the 5.5 million people already targeted under the 2026 Humanitarian Response Plan, which requires
US$632 million in funding.
Impact on infrastructure
 Authorities report at least 856 affected buildings, including 190 that have collapsed.
 As part of recovery and reconstruction planning, authorities have identified 40 sites in La Guaira
State, covering approximately 584,000 square metres, for the development of housing projects
intended for affected populations.
United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 2
 An initial assessment by the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) indicates
that direct damage to housing and infrastructure amounts to approximately US$37 billion. Most of
the damage, estimated at around US$24 billion, is concentrated in housing, businesses, schools,
hospitals, and public facilities. Meanwhile, preliminary estimates by UNDP indicate direct physical
damage of US$6.7 billion, equivalent to 6 per cent of GDP.
National response
 The Government response remains focused on search and rescue operations, as well as assistance
to affected people.
 According to authorities, the response continues with 107 transitional camps supporting affected
populations, with a capacity of 25,152 people and a current occupancy of 20,936 people. As of
14 July, 40 camps are located in Caracas, 29 in Miranda, 28 in La Guaira, and 10 in Aragua.
 Authorities are advancing a unified registration process for affected families in transitional camps
through the collection of biometric and contact information to support assistance management, social
support programmes and housing solutions.
 The Government of Venezuela announced the creation of an initial reconstruction fund equivalent to
US$200 million.
 A psychosocial support hotline remains available for affected people: 0800-AYUDA-01.
 A digital form has been launched by the National Council for Persons with Disabilities (CONAPDIS)
to support a timely and inclusive response in affected areas.
 Mechanisms have been established to locate missing persons (www.localizapacientes.com) and to
report affected individuals (0-800-RESCATE).
 School activities remain suspended in affected municipalities across the states of Aragua (Santiago
Mariño, Girardot, Ocumare de la Costa de Oro and Tovar); Carabobo (Juan José Mora, Puerto
Cabello, Naguanagua and Valencia); Falcón (José Laurencio Silva); La Guaira (Vargas); the Capital
District (Libertador); and Miranda (Chacao, Baruta, El Hatillo, Sucre, Plaza, Zamora, Acevedo, Brión,
Buroz, Páez, Andrés Bello and Pedro Gual).
Situation by state
Capital District (Caracas) and Miranda
 In Chacao municipality, Miranda state, authorities confirmed 68 deaths and the collapse of four
buildings. Of the structures assessed, 46 have been classified as red-tagged and are considered
uninhabitable.
Response actions: Organizations such as Tinta Violeta, FUNDANA and World Vision are providing
protection support to affected families, particularly through psychosocial assistance.
La Guaira
 Authorities and humanitarian organizations continue strengthening the response in La Guaira’s
transitional camps through the expansion of multisectoral services, improvements in accommodation
conditions and coordinated assistance management. The distribution of essential items, food
assistance, protection activities, health and psychosocial support interventions, as well as actions to
improve access to safe water, sanitation, connectivity and community infrastructure, continue.
Carabobo and Yaracuy (epicentral zone)
 In Carabobo, the most significant impacts continue to be concentrated in Juan José Mora
municipality (Morón parish). In Yaracuy, particularly in Veroes municipality and other localities near
the epicentral area, homes have been reported as destroyed or at high risk. Recent assessments
have identified priority needs in protection, mental health and psychosocial support, health, shelter,
water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), and food security.
Response actions: Five organizations (Venezuelan Red Cross, CESAP, Tierra Viva, Cáritas Morón
and Empodérame) are providing response in health, food, water and the distribution of humanitarian
assistance.
United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 3
Falcón (Tucacas – Silva municipality)
 The emergency remains concentrated in Silva Municipality (Tucacas and Boca de Aroa). A
magnitude 3.3 earthquake with its epicentre in Boca de Aroa renewed concerns over the weekend
and prompted preventive evacuations along the eastern coast of the state. Soil liquefaction
associated with the two earthquakes continues to affect 87 houses in the parish, impacting 252
people.
 Boca de Yaracuy Bridge remains the most severely damaged transport infrastructure, and plans are
underway to establish a temporary detour while reconstruction takes place. La Pava, El Paují and
Punta Brava bridges remain operational under speed restrictions and controls on heavy vehicle
traffic. Technical teams continue monitoring water levels in the Aroa River and Los Ingleses channel
due to the risk of seasonal flooding, amid a multi-hazard scenario.
Response actions: Protection Cluster training activities continue, alongside water, sanitation and
hygiene (WASH) interventions and psychosocial support activities in Boca de Aroa and Palmasola,
implemented by ACH, Azul Positivo, IOM, Centroccidente, ODISEF and AVSI in coordination with
regional authorities. Training on psychological first aid requested by Civil Protection for
approximately 300 officials is also progressing.
Other states
 Apure: Approximately 250 displaced people from the central coastal region remain in the state. The
Local Coordination Forum (LCF) continues to monitor the situation and provide multisectoral
assistance, including psychological first aid.
 Bolívar: Response efforts for families arriving in the state continue. VEN 911 maintains reception,
registration and comprehensive assistance mechanisms, including psychosocial support and
medical assessments, while institutional response capacity is being strengthened through
psychological first aid training for officials. Temporary accommodation remains available for 41
displaced families (127 people, including 60 adults, 10 older persons, 42 children and 15
adolescents), with the VEN 911 facility in Caroní serving as the main transitional camp. Coordination
between authorities and humanitarian actors continues to strengthen case follow-up and assistance
to affected families.
 Delta Amacuro: Preparations are being reinforced to assist affected people expected to arrive in
the state on 15 July. Planned actions include the provision of immediate food assistance for the first
72 hours by WFP, the distribution of hygiene kits by Cáritas Delta Amacuro, and food baskets for
families with children by World Vision. Tierra Viva is also assessing the distribution of children's kits.
Together with UNICEF, mechanisms are being reviewed to provide education kits to out-of-school
children and facilitate their enrolment in alternative learning spaces. The inclusion of reunified
families in WFP food assistance programmes is also under consideration. In addition, the Directorate
of Social Development is being trained in the use of a registration tool.
 Sucre: Cáritas Carúpano trained more than 241 people from various institutions in psychological
first aid, in coordination with the Carúpano Municipal Government through the Fundación Carúpano.
 Táchira: Mobile teams from IOM and ODISEF assisted 11 people on the move at the San Cristóbal
bus terminal (five women, three men and three children), providing psychological first aid and dignity
kits.
 Zulia: Triage and assistance for displaced people continue at the Maracaibo bus terminal, in
coordination with ASONACOP and the Venezuelan Red Cross, to facilitate safe transportation.
 Trujillo and Lara: Local Coordination Forums remain active, and previously reported monitoring
and relief item collection activities continue, including follow-up on assistance and protection risks
affecting people on the move.
Humanitarian coordination
 OCHA, together with the Humanitarian Coordinator and in coordination with national authorities,
continues to coordinate the humanitarian response with the United Nations and partner
organizations, prioritizing actions in health, shelter, food security, WASH, logistics and protection.
United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 4
 UNDAC and OCHA continued supporting Civil Protection in strengthening emergency coordination
and information management capacities, including technical exchanges on USAR coordination
mechanisms and operational tracking tools.
 A total of 71 search and rescue teams from 31 countries, comprising 2,786 personnel and 216 search
dogs, were deployed to the worst-affected areas in support of rescue operations. The total includes
teams that are currently being demobilized.
 OCHA continued strengthening coordination with the private sector to support response and early
recovery efforts, promoting engagement with specialized actors in areas such as logistics, debris
management, infrastructure rehabilitation and reconstruction planning through existing coordination
mechanisms between the United Nations and the private sector.
 Venezuelan authorities requested the activation of the Post-Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA)
within the framework of the United Nations system and with the support of UNDP. In line with the
internationally recognized PDNA methodology, the corresponding coordination efforts with relevant
counterparts will be advanced.
 Authorities informed the activation of a special mechanism to expedite the processing of a “Work
Visa for Special Situations” through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The procedure will be carried out
online under the coordination of the Office of the Vice Minister for Multilateral Affairs and the Consular
Affairs Office. It is intended for foreign personnel of international organizations, as well as United
Nations staff, deploying to Venezuela in support of the response to the earthquake emergency.
Initial humanitarian response
Food Security
 Since the beginning of the emergency response, WFP has reached 67,520 people with food
assistance. On 14 July, WFP continued supporting populations affected by the earthquake through
the distribution of family food baskets and the provision of hot meals. A total of 750 family food
baskets were distributed in communities across Sucre parish in Libertador municipality (Distrito
Capital) and Carlos Soublette parish (La Guaira), reaching 3,000 people. In addition, 125 family food
baskets were provided to support meal preparation in temporary shelters located in Catia La Mar
and Carlos Soublette parish, benefiting 500 people. These baskets contain essential dry food
commodities and cover approximately 75 percent of household food requirements for 30 days.
 Furthermore, through its partners, WFP provided 6,756 hot meals (lunch and dinner) for
approximately 3,400 people across three transitional camps: the José María Vargas Sports Stadium,
the César Nieves Baseball Stadium, and the Playa Grande community, helping ensure continued
access to food for displaced and affected families.
Health
 As of 12 July, 22 international Emergency Medical Teams (EMTs) had been deployed, were
mobilizing or were demobilizing in earthquake-affected areas, supporting the health response
through emergency medical care, field hospitals, mobile health services and specialized assistance,
and complementing national capacities.
 IOM has provided health services to 4,640 people across priority transitional camps in La Guaira.
 UNICEF continued operating its health point in the Playa Grande transitional camp, where it provided
care to 21 people (eight women, nine men, two girls and two boys). UNICEF also announced that,
as of 15 July, the facility will be dedicated exclusively to immunization activities to strengthen
vaccination coverage within the transitorial camp.
 Through its partner Ven Da Tu Mano (VDTM), UNFPA delivered sexual and reproductive health
(SRH) services in the José María Vargas Sports Complex, César Nieves Stadium and Playa Grande
transitional camps, reaching 125 people through individual consultations. During the reporting
period, teams conducted 31 antenatal care visits, inserted 84 subdermal contraceptive implants, and
administered 10 injectable contraceptives. In addition, 172 SRH counselling and awareness-raising
sessions were carried out.
United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 5
 In the Playa Grande transitional camp, Project HOPE conducted 39 medical consultations and
distributed medicines, while Ven Da Tu Mano provided 69 primary health-care consultations,
including general medicine, paediatrics, gynaecology and internal medicine.
 The Spanish Red Cross established an emergency clinic in La Guaira, providing health services to
200 people through service points located at the baseball field and San José Hospital. The main
needs addressed included chronic diseases, earthquake-related injuries and mental health support.
The operation is being implemented in coordination with the Venezuelan Red Cross and continues
to provide assistance to affected populations.
 Fundación Proyecto Maniapure (FPM) conducted a multidisciplinary mobile health outreach in Punta
Care community (Naiguatá parish, La Guaira), providing 82 services to 76 people. Services included
primary health care, internal medicine, family medicine, obstetrics and gynaecology, nutrition,
physiotherapy, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), sexual and reproductive health
(SRH), and the distribution of medicines. Assessments identified a high demand for care related to
chronic conditions, particularly hypertension and diabetes among older persons, as well as cases of
diarrhoeal diseases. Hygiene kits were also distributed based on identified needs.
 International Medical Corps (IMC) continues to deploy Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) across La
Guaira State, providing free medical consultations, medicines and mental health services through
three service points: the La Lucha MMU, located at Farmatodo in Catia La Mar; the Playa Grande
MMU, located at Farmatodo in Playa Grande; and the Type 1 EMT, located at the Catia La Mar
Passenger Terminal near Dr. Alfredo Machado Outpatient Clinic. IMC also continues to cover
affected communities and other priority locations to strengthen health response capacity. Teams
include three general practitioners, three nurses, two paediatricians, one obstetrics and gynaecology
specialist, support staff, and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) personnel.
 Between 1 and 13 July 2026, IMC's mobile medical units conducted a total of 1,408 consultations in
earthquake-affected communities in La Guaira. Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) accounted for
the largest proportion of consultations, with 656 cases (46.6 per cent), followed by communicable
diseases, with 526 consultations (37.4 per cent). In addition, teams provided 90 mental health and
psychosocial support consultations (6.4 per cent), 86 sexual and reproductive health consultations
(6.1 per cent) and 50 trauma and injury consultations (3.6 per cent). These figures indicate sustained
demand for primary health care, chronic disease management, communicable disease surveillance,
sexual and reproductive health services, psychosocial support and injury care, underscoring the
importance of maintaining essential services and community follow-up in the most heavily affected
areas.
Logistics and Telecommunications
 The Logistics Working Group (LWG) supported the transportation of medical supplies in La Guaira
for Médecins du Monde through common logistics services provided free of charge. Coordination
with partners continues to facilitate the provision of storage and transport services in line with the
LWG's available capacities.
. Nutrition
 UNICEF established three breastfeeding support spaces in three transitional camps, providing
guidance and assistance to breastfeeding mothers.
Protection (including Children and Gender-Based Violence)
 IOM has provided protection assistance to 216 people through the transitional camps supported by
the organization.
 UNHCR continued providing legal counselling, psychosocial support, documentation assistance and
referrals to specialized services in transitional camps across La Guaira. On 14 July, a total of 51
people, including children and adolescents, participated in protection activities, legal assistance,
United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 6
case management, psychosocial support, counselling and referrals to specialized services in the
Playa Grande, César Nieves Stadium and José María Vargas Sports Complex transitional camps.
 UNHCR supported coordination among government institutions responsible for the management
and handling of protection cases that will provide services in the César Nieves Stadium transitional
camp. As part of these efforts, referral pathways were strengthened and a directory of focal points
was established to facilitate affected populations’ access to specialized protection services.
 Through its partner FUNDAINIL, UNICEF provided protection services in the Playa Grande
transitional camp, reaching 40 children and adolescents and 12 adults through Child-Friendly
Spaces, recreational, sports and play-based activities, as well as awareness-raising activities on the
prevention of child sexual abuse, the right to positive treatment and positive parenting. One case
was also referred to the child protection system.
 UNFPA carried out gender-based violence (GBV) prevention and response activities in the José
María Vargas Sports Complex, César Nieves Stadium and Playa Grande transitional camps,
reaching 94 people through community awareness-raising activities, including adolescents, pregnant
women and breastfeeding women. In addition, UNFPA provided five psychosocial support
interventions, followed up on two protection cases, and conducted awareness-raising activities on
safe referral mechanisms and access to specialized services.
Shelter and Non-Food Items
 Since the onset of the earthquake response, IOM has supported the management and coordination
of five identified transitional camps in La Guaira, reaching 6,290 unique individuals through the
delivery of 9,876 services. Activities include site management and coordination, registration,
community engagement, information management and case referrals, facilitating displaced
populations’ access to essential services.
 In parallel, IOM continues to support improvements in transitional camps, including shelter upgrades
and enhancements to basic site infrastructure. The organization is also strengthening coordination
with authorities and humanitarian partners to help improve living conditions and facilitate affected
families’ access to assistance. As part of the effort, IOM has distributed core relief items to 4,244
people.
 To date, in the José María Vargas Sports Complex transitional camp, UNHCR has installed a total
of 30 floodlights to improve lighting in communal areas and mitigate protection risks.
Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH)
 UNICEF and its partners continue to provide 80,000 litres of safe water per day across the three
identified transitional camps in La Guaira, benefiting approximately 3,500 people. In addition, as of
12 July, more than 1,730 hygiene kits had been distributed, reaching over 6,900 people.
 UNICEF also continues to strengthen sanitation and hygiene conditions in transitional camps through
the installation of at least 86 portable toilets and 48 handwashing stations, as well as the regular
cleaning and maintenance of these facilities. As of 12 July, UNICEF had also distributed more than
300 waste containers, along with garbage bags and basic cleaning supplies, and continues to
support hygiene promotion activities.
 International Medical Corps (IMC) continues to support access to safe water through the provision
of drinking water via water trucks.
Humanitarian financing and contributions
 The United Nations humanitarian chief, Tom Fletcher, announced an additional appeal under the
Humanitarian Response Plan for Venezuela. The appeal outlines the multisectoral needs of 1.3
million people over the next six months. To reach those in need, US$298 million is required, in
addition to the US$632 million requested at the beginning of the year.
 IOM launched a US$98 million appeal to assist 850,000 people and support 140 entities over the
next six months. PAHO/WHO launched an emergency appeal for nearly US$24 million to support
health response and early recovery activities over the next six months and released US$1.5 million
from the Contingency Fund for Emergencies. WFP launched an initial appeal for US$80 million
United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 7
to provide food assistance to 500,000 people over a six-month period. UNHCR requires
US$14.8 million to support up to 30,000 affected people over the next six months.
 A shipment from Switzerland arrived on 13 July carrying one metric ton of medical supplies.
 The Government of Italy allocated US$5.7 million to support the humanitarian response to the
earthquakes, helping deliver life-saving assistance, protection and access to essential services for
affected populations through AICS, WFP and IFRC.
 Caritas Spain announced an increase in its contribution to €1 million to support the earthquake
response in Venezuela, including the €300,000 mobilized during the first days of the emergency.
This support is complemented by the deployment of representatives from Caritas Spain and other
Cáritas network organizations in the country, providing technical and coordination support in WASH,
food security, livelihoods, risk management and shelter.
 A new European Union Humanitarian Air Bridge flight landed on 13 July carrying 29 metric tonnes
of shelter and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) supplies. The cargo included European Union-
funded assistance for IOM, Irish-funded support for GOAL Global, and UNICEF supplies.
 The Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) allocated US$15 million to support a multisectoral
response, alongside the activation of the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund (VHF). Norway contributed
to support the response through CERF.
 The United States announced a US$100 million contribution to the VHF, in addition to a further
US$100 million in bilateral funding for response operations implemented by IOM, WFP, UNICEF,
International Medical Corps, Catholic Relief Services, Samaritan’s Purse, Proyecto Esperanza and
the Red Cross.
 Germany and the Republic of Korea contributed US$5 million and US$1.25 million, respectively, to
the VHF to support humanitarian action in the country.
 On 14 July, the Republic of Korea announced an additional allocation of US$3.5 million in
humanitarian assistance. Of this amount, US$3 million will be channelled through UNDP to support
debris removal activities, while the remainder will be provided in-kind, specifically through 30 metric
tons of temporary shelters (family tents). The Republic of Korea had previously allocated
US$1.25 million to WFP and US$2.5 million to UNICEF in support of the humanitarian response in
Venezuela.
 Japan allocated US$3.5 million to support the earthquake response. The funding will provide
humanitarian assistance in key sectors, including food security, health care, shelter and non-food
items, through WFP, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)
and IOM.
 The European Union allocated €5 million to support the emergency response, in addition to the €52
million already allocated this year for humanitarian operations in the country.
 Australia announced a US$2 million contribution to support the provision of food, shelter, healthcare
and access to safe water through IFRC and WFP.
 Switzerland announced a contribution of CHF 2.5 million to support the response.
 Sweden allocated SEK 25 million to support the humanitarian response through food assistance,
water, temporary shelter, protection and family reunification programmes implemented by WFP,
UNHCR and Save the Children.
 Denmark announced an additional contribution of DKK 11 million to support the humanitarian
response, including DKK 10 million through UNHCR and DKK 1 million through DanChurchAid and
the Danish Red Cross.
 The Disasters Emergency Committee (DEC) announced an initial allocation of £7.5 million for the
earthquake response in Venezuela, including £2 million contributed by the United Kingdom
Government through UK Aid Match. The funds will be implemented by DEC member agencies and
their local partners to support the humanitarian response.
 As part of the support provided by UNDAC, the team includes a private sector coordination specialist
to strengthen business engagement in response and recovery efforts. A private sector contributions
tracker for the Venezuela earthquake response is available at https://ven-
eq.connectingbusiness.org, together with a briefing note for the private sector outlining opportunities
for engagement. Focal point: sanchez21@un.org.
 OCHA continues to coordinate with donors and partners to ensure rapid, strategic and needs-based
allocation of resources.
United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
www.unocha.org

OCHA | 8

documents.body_text:
**Reporte de situación N.º 21**  
**Terremotos en Venezuela**  
**14 de julio de 2026**  
**Hora: 9:00 pm**

**Destacados**

- Tras los sismos de magnitud 7,2 y 7,5 del 24 de junio (18:00 hora local), **las autoridades reportan más de 1.200 réplicas.**
- Balance oficial: **4.734 personas fallecidas y 16.740 heridas.**
- **6.462 personas han sido rescatadas.**
- **Se lanzó un llamamiento adicional por US$298 millones para ampliar la respuesta a los terremotos y atender las necesidades de 1,3 millones de personas durante los próximos seis meses.**
- El Sistema de Naciones Unidas y sus organizaciones socias, en coordinación con el gobierno, responden con acciones multisectoriales y continuarán ampliando la asistencia a las personas afectadas.

**Situación general**

Venezuela enfrenta una emergencia nacional tras dos sismos consecutivos de gran magnitud (7,2 y 7,5) ocurridos el 24 de junio (18:00, hora local) en la región centro-norte, con epicentro sobre el eje San Felipe - Yumare - Montalbán (Yaracuy/Carabobo). **Las autoridades reportan 1.275 réplicas.**

A 20 días de los terremotos, las autoridades reportan un balance de **4.734 personas fallecidas, 16.740 personas heridas y 6.462 personas rescatadas** desde el inicio de la emergencia. Asimismo, indicaron que **17.907 personas perdieron sus viviendas.**

La respuesta gubernamental mantiene el foco en las labores de búsqueda, la gestión de los campamentos transitorios y la atención de las personas afectadas. Naciones Unidas y sus organizaciones socias, en articulación con las autoridades, realizan acciones multisectoriales para las personas afectadas y continuarán ampliando la respuesta. El Subsecretario General de las Naciones Unidas para Asuntos Humanitarios y Coordinador del Socorro de Emergencia, Tom Fletcher, **anunció una adenda al Plan de Respuesta Humanitaria por 298 millones de dólares, destinada a atender las necesidades multisectoriales de 1,3 millones de personas durante los próximos seis meses**. Esto se suma a la meta de 5,5 millones de personas que ya contemplaba atenderse con el Plan este 2026, para lo que se requieren 632 millones de dólares.

comercios, escuelas, hospitales e instalaciones públicas. Entre tanto, estimaciones preliminares de
PNUD indican daños físicos directos por 6.700 millones de dólares, equivalentes al 6 % del PIB.
Respuesta nacional
 La respuesta gubernamental se mantiene centrada en las labores de búsqueda y rescate, así como
en la atención de las personas afectadas.

la atención de personas afectadas, con capacidad para 25.152 personas y una ocupación de
20.936 personas. Hasta el 14 de julio, 40 campamentos se encuentran instalados en Caracas, 29
en Miranda, 28 en La Guaira, y 10 en Aragua.

transitorios, mediante la recopilación de datos biométricos y de contacto para apoyar la gestión de
la asistencia, los programas de apoyo social y las soluciones habitacionales.
 El Gobierno venezolano anunció la creación de un fondo inicial de reconstrucción equivalente a 200
millones de dólares.
 Disponible la línea de apoyo psicológico para las personas afectadas: 0800-AYUDA-01.
 Se habilitó un formulario digital del Consejo Nacional para las Personas con Discapacidad
(Conapdis) para coordinar una respuesta oportuna e inclusiva en las zonas afectadas.
 Se habilitaron mecanismos para la localización de personas desaparecidas
(www.localizapacientes.com) y el reporte de personas afectadas (0-800-RESCATE).

Seguridad Alimentaria
